job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

response.passage: Aarav and his grandfather sat on their balcony in Delhi, watching the sunset. Aarav asked, 'Dadu, does the Sun travel behind the Earth to hide at night?' His grandfather smiled and explained that the Earth spins on its own invisible axis, which causes day and night. He clarified that this axis is just an imaginary line, not a physical pole. Aarav then asked about the changing weather. 'Is it summer because we are closer to the Sun?' he wondered. Dadu shook his head, explaining that seasons change due to the Earth's tilt and its revolution around the Sun, not because of the distance. He added that the Earth takes about 365 and a quarter days to complete one orbit. To keep our calendar accurate, we add an extra day to February every four years, which we call a leap year. Aarav realized that the Earth is a complex, moving home. He felt amazed thinking about the planet spinning silently while they sat there. The cool evening breeze reminded him that even though the Earth is always in motion, they feel perfectly still on its surface. It was a beautiful lesson about the world they live in.
response.summary: The passage explains that day and night are caused by the Earth's rotation on an imaginary axis. It also clarifies that seasons depend on the Earth's tilt and revolution, while leap years account for the extra time in the Earth's orbit.
